headline: Set October parking rate at $4/hour with 20% resident discount and $100 daily fine; authorized $200,000 Mass Clean Energy Center harbor planning grant.
summary: Members updated the Salem Ferry Terminal building design, which now has an elevation of 14’ 4”. Members voted to set October parking at $4/hour and the October fine at $100/day. They also authorized a $200,000 grant agreement with the Mass Clean Energy Center.
decisions: Approved setting the base parking rate to $4/hour with a 20% discount for residents during October. The motion passed.
Approved setting the fine rate to $100/day during October. The motion passed.
Approved empowering the Port Director, Capt. McHugh, to enter into a $200,000 grant agreement with the CEC for harbor planning. The motion passed.
Approved the minutes for the August 6th meeting. The motion passed.

SALEM HARBOR PORT AUTHORITY
98 WASHINGTON STREET, SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS  01970 
   (978) 619-5685 PLANNING 
(978) 741-0098 HARBORMASTER 
 
MEETING MINUTES: September 3, 2026 
A
 public meeting of the Salem Harbor Port Authority was convened at 5:00 pm via Zoom web 
conference.  
Me
mbers present: Councilor Turowski, Capt. Ryan, Fed Atkins, and Philip Pelletier 
Others Present: Capt. Bill McHugh – Harbormaster, Daniel Collins – Planning Department 
C
all to Order 
Capt. Ryan called the meeting to order at 5:00pm. Roll was called. 
C
hairperson Designation  
Mr. Collins read a letter from Mayor Pangallo appointing Capt. Ryan as Chairperson. 
P
ort Updates 
• Terminal Building Project Presentation
Aaron Udy, Tim Arnold, Deborah Fennick, and Cyrus Gagaza were present:
o Capt. McHugh noted that they are trying to work through design and cost containment. They
will review the timeline.
o Capt. McHugh noted that they received the Order of Conditions from the Conservation
Commission and they went before the ZBA for the required variance. The next presentation will
be before the Planning Board. They are also working on the Chapter 91 license. He estimated
that they are about a year away from going out to bid for the project.
o Mr. Collins reviewed the timeline.
o Ms. Fennick reviewed the program summary. The Salem Ferry Terminal will serve as a
p
ermanent, resilient and modern gateway hub for waterborne transportation.
o Key components include passenger services, operational capacity, leasable office spaces,
applying for Chapter 91 and Waterways Licensing, training and event spaces, and facility
security/IT space.
o The key purposes of the development are for port operations and marine services and design for
resiliency and sustainability.
o T
he existing conditions plan was reviewed. The reclaimed granite is planned for use at the site.
o The proposed site circulation plan was shared and reviewed.
o The elevation of the building has changed to 14’ 4”  after discussions with local and state
building code officials. They decided to take a more conservative approach after learning that
the 16’ 2” elevation may be overbuilt. They are complying with C-ROD requirements. They will
als
o be speaking with the City’s Building Inspector. The hope is the shift will help with cost
containment as there will be a reduction in the number of micro-piles.
o With this change the building won’t be as high, and the costs will be reduced overall.
o M
r. Udy reviewed the landscape plantings and the layout plans. The layout has not changed
s
ignificantly since last presented.
o The separate men’s/women’s restroom has been changed to a gender-neutral bathroom. The
s
talls are full height. It is fully compliant with the building code.
o The velocity zone and access diagram was shown indicating the edge of the concrete, pedestrian
access, emergency vehicle access, and area for future solar panels.
o Renderings of the exterior views were shared and reviewed showing the building design and
landscaping. The materials were reviewed. Interior views of the building were shared.
o T
he handrails remain with the reduced building height, but they are reduced.
o C
ouncilor Turowski said the building is beautiful and glad it’s taking shape. She appreciated the
f
eedback being accepted regarding the gender-neutral bathrooms.
• Z
BA Memorandum
o Mr. Collins reported that the ZBA had a condition that petitioner submit a letter of permission
from the owner of 71 Derby Street verifying that construction of the Ferry Terminal Building can
take place at 67/71 Derby Street to the Planning Department prior to receiving a building
permit. Mr. Collins noted that the SPA is the petitioner and the owner, but it is required to
satisfy the special condition.
o Capt. McHugh said the letter is procedural and that he will draft a letter for the ZBA.
P
assport Parking Initiative  
Capt. McHugh reported that the sign will be put on the property next Tuesday. The sign will announce 
the pay to park via the PassPort app with an effective date of September 15th.  
C
apt. Ryan said he thinks the timing is good given the uptick in traffic leading up to Halloween. Councilor 
Turowski recommended sending an alert out to the neighborhood when the sign goes up. Capt. McHugh 
will coordinate the wording.  
C
apt. McHugh said he would like to see a vote on the parking rates. He reiterated his concern about the 
lot not being the cheapest place to park during the month of October. There is a 20% discount for 
residents. He said sees rates as high as $50/day during October. He would propose rates at $4/hour 
during October. He would also like to change the fine during October. Fines are $25 and it would be 
cheaper to pay the fine that pay for parking and suggested the fine be raised to $100 during October. 
The $100 fine would be for each day.  
C
ouncilor Turowski motioned, seconded by Mr. Pelletier, to set the base parking rate to $4/hour with a 
20% discount for residents during the month of October. The motion passed.   
M
r. Pelletier motioned, seconded by Councilor Turowski, to set the fine rate to $100/day during the 
month of October. The motion passed.   
C
EC Harbor Planning Grant 
Mr. Collins reported that the are looking for approval from the Board to move forward on a $200,000 
grant agreement with the Mass Clean Energy Center for future navigation dredging planning and 
development of navigation models. They are looking to collect all the existing information they have and 
identify gaps. Capt. McHugh said there is a sewer transmission line that runs underneath the channel 
and close to the turning basin. He said they want to make sure they have all the points cataloged. They 
would also like to understand the maximum threat vessel in terms of the structures on the seabed.
M
r. Pelletier motioned, seconded by Councilor Turowski, to empower the Port Director, Capt. McHugh, 
to enter into a $200,000 grant agreement with the CEC for harbor planning. The motion passed.   
S
taff/Authority Updates 
• Harbor Master Report
Capt. McHugh reported that there was a mechanical failure on the Bowditch which took out one of the
transmissions. The original marine gear was saved, so it was used to replace the gear that failed. BHC
will be rebuilding the gear that failed as it was only four years old.
C
apt. McHugh said this has been an active yacht season. 
P
ublic Comment 
There were no members of the public wishing to comment. 
C
ouncilor Turowski noted that there will be a dedication for the new art installation on Blaney Street 
Wharf on Thursday, September 24th at 5pm. Capt. McHugh noted that SPA members will receive an 
email regarding the event.  
A
pproval of the Minutes 
Councilor Turowski motioned, seconded by Mr. Pelletier, to approve the minutes for the August 6th 
meeting. The motion passed.   
A
djournment 
Councilor Turowski motioned, seconded by Mr. Pelletier, to adjourn the meeting. The motion passed.  
Approved by the Salem Harbor Port Authority at the meeting held on October 15, 2026.

The new Salem Ferry Terminal will serve as a permanent, resilient and modern gateway hub for 
waterborne transportation.

Key Purposes of Development
Port Operations
• Ferry operations and larger passenger vessels are the primary function of terminal
• Flexible to accommodate other marine services: vessel business, excursions
• Ensure orderly and safe passenger movement and access for emergency services
